integrity: The proof checks all alternatives in the source theorem. A periodic orbit is finite and therefore rules out boundary escape; a recurrent interior point also rules out boundary escape. In the bounded convergence branch, a periodic or recurrent point must equal the unique fixed point. A nontrivial cycle therefore forces the only remaining bounded branch, namely the isometric uniformly quasiconformal homeomorphism case.
scientific_limitations: The result is a structural consequence of the new Denjoy--Wolff dichotomy for uniformly quasiregular self-maps of the unit ball. It does not classify periodic or recurrent points inside the uniformly quasiconformal homeomorphism branch, quantify convergence rates, or extend the classification to globally defined uniformly quasiregular maps.
title: Periodic and recurrent rigidity for non-elliptic uniformly quasiregular ball maps
